docRequirement: `permissions.md:507` and `settings.md:328`/`:1169-1191` bind us to a managed-settings-only key spelled exactly `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`, whose value is either `true` or an array naming a subset of exactly four surfaces — `skills`, `agents`, `hooks`, `mcp`. For each locked surface the client must skip user-level and project-level sources and load only plugin-provided and managed ones: `skills` blocks `~/.claude/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` while bundled skills, plugin skills and skills in the managed policy directory still load; `agents` blocks `~/.claude/agents/` and `.claude/agents/` while plugin, built-in and managed-directory agents still load; `hooks` blocks hooks in user, project and local `settings.json` while plugin and managed hooks still load; `mcp` blocks servers in `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json` while plugin and `managed-mcp.json` servers still load. One parse rule is stated explicitly: "Surface names that a Claude Code version doesn't recognize are ignored rather than failing the settings file."
current:

Only the `hooks` quarter has an equivalent, under a DIFFERENT key. `allowManagedHooksOnly` (managed-policy.ts:177, parsed :1329-1332, read by `isManagedHooksOnly` :1598-1600) is resolved at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:11284-11287 and enforced in `buildPinnedAgentAutomationSystem` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-automations.ts:94-106, 113-125, 144) where the native and project hook tiers are skipped whole and plugin hooks survive only when force-enabled; the plugin-candidate half runs at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:739-748. `disableAllHooks` (managed-policy.ts:191) and `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` (managed-policy.ts:203, read at SessionManager.ts:4101, :14274, :16248) are the other two managed-only locks that exist.

Nothing locks the ORIGIN of skills or agents. `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` discovers them from four user-controlled tiers: global `~/.nessy-agent/skills` and `~/.nessy-agent/agents` plus the portable `~/.agents/skills` layer (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:903-905), workspace `<workspaceRoot>/skills` and `<workspaceRoot>/*.md` agents (native-sources.ts:947-948), trusted-project `<project>/.nessy-agent/skills` and `<project>/.nessy-agent/agents` (native-sources.ts:1016-1017), and the nested portable `.agents/skills` ancestor layers (native-sources.ts:1062-1064). `~/.nessy-agent` is the USER's config dir (packages/shared/src/config/paths.ts:18-21), not an admin tier — `getManagedSkillsRoot()` (packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:27-29) means the app-managed seed root, not managed settings. The only managed filter over that inventory is the record filter at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:692-715, which drops MCP records by identity and nothing else, and returns early for non-Pi turns at :699. Our admin channel carries no skill or agent definitions at all: the managed document is a single `managed-policy.json` plus a `managed-policy.d/` drop-in dir (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52, :62-67), never scanned for components, the same emptiness recorded for hooks at packages/shared/src/config/managed-approval.ts:16.

The `mcp` surface already has an owner ruling: docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:95 files `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` with `mcp` as `documented, not implemented — a settings key we do not carry`.
divergence:
Three separate deltas, only one of which is cosmetic.

(1) The KEY NAME is absent, not merely unenforced. An administrator writing the documented `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` gets it stripped as unknown (managed-policy.ts:727-733); there is no alias, no partial parse. So even the surface we do enforce is unreachable through the documented spelling.

(2) The `hooks` surface has the right BEHAVIOUR under the wrong KEY. `allowManagedHooksOnly` produces exactly the doc's hooks row (user/project hook tiers dropped, force-enabled plugin hooks kept). This is a key-name-only divergence for that quarter: mapping `strictPluginOnlyCustomization: ['hooks']` onto the existing `managedHookLock.enabled` is a one-line OR at SessionManager.ts:11284.

(3) The `skills` and `agents` surfaces have NO mechanism of any kind — no key, no filter, no predicate. This is the real gap. Nothing in `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` constrains the ORIGIN of a skill or an agent; `allowedPluginKeys`/`deniedPluginKeys`/`enabledPlugins` narrow plugins only, and narrowing plugins does not touch a native record. `availableModels` restricts which model a skill may use, never where the skill came from — an identically-shaped key in the same file that is not this control.

One parse rule also diverges in advance: the page requires unknown surface names to be IGNORED, while our list parser `list()` (managed-policy.ts:783-797) throws on any entry that fails validation, so a naive reuse of `grant`/`restrict` would fail the whole key on a future surface name — the opposite of what the page specifies.

Finally, the `mcp` surface is genuinely narrower than the doc rather than absent: `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` can deny named/URL/command-identified servers from native records (storage-runtime.ts:704-713), but there is no "only plugin and managed servers" pole — `allowedMcpServers: []` blocks plugin servers too (storage-runtime.ts:732-733).

blastRadius:
Crosses a PERSISTENCE and a WIRE boundary, so this is a risk trigger in this repo. `ManagedPiPolicyV1` is not a local type: the same document arrives from a host-owned file plus `managed-policy.d/` fragments (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts) AND from a server-fetched payload that is salvaged and cached at mode 0600 (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts), composed by packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts and resolved by packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127-139. A field added to the schema and not to that path fails the reachability property pinned in storage-runtime-delivered-policy.test.ts:160,183 by construction. `isManagedPolicyTightening` (managed-policy.ts:625-640) decides whether a mid-session re-read applies immediately or waits for a turn boundary, and `managedPolicyEquals`/`canonicalPolicyJson` (:600-602, :656-668) hash the whole key set.

On the enforcement side the filter feeds `EffectiveCapabilitySnapshot`, which projects THREE ways (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:1-12): `toAgentRuntime` for the agent, and `toComposerCatalog`/`toUserCatalog` for the renderer. Locked skills and agents therefore disappear from the Skills and Agents lists in the UI as well as from the turn — intended (the doc says the sources are skipped), but it is a visible product change, not a silent one. Readers of `view.skills`: packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:1062, :2124, :2288, :2345, :2410, :2513, :2712; packages/shared/src/capabilities/skill-resource-resolver.ts:118; packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:366; packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:566; packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4537, :10964, :12060, :12087; packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:206. Readers of `view.agents`: base-agent.ts:2557, harness-manifest.ts:367, runtime-agent-definition.ts:477. `harness-manifest.ts` hashes both into the Pi harness manifest, so a locked fleet gets a different manifest generation.

Two boundaries the change must not assume it covers. The workspace BROWSE pool is provider-neutral by contract (`WorkspaceMcpPoolRegistry.buildResolveContext`, recorded in docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md § 'The provider guard, and what it leaves open'), so an `mcp` surface enforced only in the capability inputs still lets the Sources UI connect a blocked server. And imported plugin paths are untouched: the Claude and Codex format adapters keep contributing skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from PLUGIN bundles, which is exactly what every locked surface must continue to load.
userImpact:
For an administrator: deploying `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` in `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json` (or via the server-delivered payload) does nothing at all. The key is stripped as unknown and `nessy-general-agent doctor` reports `invalid managed Pi policy key: strictPluginOnlyCustomization` with disposition `stripped` — so the failure is visible rather than silent, but the fleet stays unlocked. An admin who copies a working Claude Code managed-settings block into Nessy gets a policy that reads as deployed and enforces nothing on three of its four surfaces.

For an end user on such a fleet: every skill in `~/.nessy-agent/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `<workspace>/skills` and a trusted project's `.nessy-agent/skills`, and every subagent in `~/.nessy-agent/agents`, `<workspace>/*.md` and `<project>/.nessy-agent/agents`, still appears in the Skills and Agents lists, is still offered to the model, and is still invocable — including a skill a repository shipped, once the project-trust dialog is accepted. The only gate is that per-user trust prompt, which is the user's decision, not the administrator's. The hooks surface is the exception: an admin who knows to reach for `allowManagedHooksOnly` instead does get the documented hooks behaviour today.
